docs.text: SpamAPI documentation ¶ Use SpamAPI to classify comments and form submissions through its REST API or WordPress plugin. Manage your API keys and usage in the SpamAPI dashboard . Integrate SpamAPI ¶ Getting started : verify a key and make your first check. API reference : endpoints, errors, and usage headers. WordPress setup : install and configure the plugin. Test mode : exercise test submissions and guaranteed spam values. Troubleshooting : diagnose common integration problems. Download the SpamAPI Anti-Spam plugin ZIP to install it through the WordPress admin. See the setup guide for configuration. Download the OpenAPI specification or an integration example: Go , JavaScript , PHP , or Python . The JavaScript example uses Node.js 24's built-in fetch . Download node.js and run it with your dashboard API key: SPAMAPI_KEY=spa_... node node.js For supported versions and vulnerability reporting, see the security policy .

docs.text: Security policy ¶ Supported versions ¶ Security fixes target the current main branch. Deployments should use the latest reviewed revision of main ; older revisions and experimental branches do not receive separate security backports. This policy covers the SpamAPI service, dashboard, and WordPress plugin. Reporting a vulnerability ¶ Report suspected SpamAPI vulnerabilities through the private vulnerability reporting form . Sign in to GitHub to submit a report. Reports are private to the reporter and maintainers handling the advisory. Include the affected component and version, impact, reproduction steps, and a minimal proof of concept using synthetic data. Never send live API keys, tokens, payment details, or customer content. Coordinate disclosure with maintainers after a fix is available, and keep exploit details out of public issues and PRs.

docs.text: API Reference ¶ Public API (API Key) ¶ Base path: /api/v1 Method Path Description POST /verify-key Validate API key POST /check Check content for spam POST /submit-spam Report false negative POST /submit-ham Report false positive GET /usage Monthly usage summary GET /sites Sites using the key Public API Responses ¶ Both feedback endpoints return HTTP 200 with a JSON acknowledgement: {"status": "ok"} GET /api/v1/usage returns the current month's quota and usage. percentage is a decimal string; resets_at is a UTC timestamp; throttled indicates that the account has reached its quota. A paid plan's quota applies until its subscription ends, including the rest of a paid period after cancellation; the account then uses the Free quota. { "limit": 100, "used": 12, "percentage": "12.00", "resets_at": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z", "throttled": false } GET /api/v1/sites returns sites , total , limit , and offset . Each site contains site , api_calls , spam , ham , missed_spam , false_positives , first_seen , and last_seen . Pagination defaults to 50 sites and is capped at 100 per request. The dashboard's sites endpoint uses its own response schema. Dashboard API (Session) ¶ Base path: /dashboard/api Method Path Description GET /account Get account PATCH /account Initiate email change GET /api-keys List keys POST /api-keys Create key DELETE /api-keys/{id} Delete key GET /usage/summary Usage summary GET /usage/history Usage history GET /sites Sites stats GET /billing/subscription Subscription POST /billing/checkout Checkout session POST /billing/portal Billing portal Authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <session-token> , using the token returned by registration or login. Account responses wrap the current user in user . Changing the account email requires both email and the current password ; the response still contains the current email until confirmation. Creating a key returns HTTP 200 with key (the full credential, shown only once) and api_key (its metadata). Listing keys returns a keys array; deleting a key returns HTTP 204 with no body. Usage history returns a history array with month , spam_checks , spam_detected , ham_detected , submit_spam , and submit_ham . The lookback defaults to six months and is capped at 24. Subscription details are wrapped in subscription . While a canceled subscription remains active, cancel_at gives its scheduled end and status is unchanged; it is absent otherwise. Checkout requires plan , success_url , and cancel_url ; the billing portal requires return_url . Redirect URLs must use the application's origin ( https://spamapi.de for the hosted service). Both endpoints return url . Auth API ¶ Base path: /auth Method Path Description POST /register Register POST /login Login POST /logout Logout GET /me Current user POST /verify Verify email POST /confirm-email-change Confirm email change POST /forgot Forgot password POST /reset Reset password Registration returns HTTP 201 ; login returns HTTP 200 . Both return user , token , and session . GET /auth/me returns user and session , and logout returns HTTP 204 with no body. Email verification and email-change confirmation accept token and return user . Forgot-password accepts email and returns HTTP 202 with {"status":"email_sent"} . Reset-password accepts token and new_password and returns the user object directly. Error Format ¶ The public and dashboard APIs use the following JSON error format. Auth handlers return a JSON error string; their rate limiter and the dashboard session middleware can return plain-text errors. { "error": "invalid_api_key", "message": "Invalid API key", "request_id": "req_123" } POST /api/v1/check returns HTTP 503 with error code detection_unavailable when the selected classifier fails or times out. This error carries no spam decision, score, or recommendation. Failed classifications do not increment classification usage or update site statistics. See troubleshooting for how to handle this response. Usage Headers ¶ X-Usage-Limit X-Usage-Used X-Usage-Remaining Rate Limit Headers ¶ X-RateLimit-Limit X-RateLimit-Remaining X-RateLimit-Reset Full OpenAPI Spec ¶ See docs/api/openapi.yaml .

docs.text: Getting Started ¶ This guide walks through verifying an API key and checking content for spam. Base URL ¶ https://spamapi.de Authentication ¶ Use an API key in the request header: X-API-Key: spa_... Replace spa_... with a SpamAPI key from the dashboard. Stripe keys beginning with sk_live_ or sk_test_ cannot authenticate SpamAPI requests. Verify Key ¶ POST /api/v1/verify-key { "api_key": "spa_..." } Check Content ¶ POST /api/v1/check { "blog": "https://example.com", "user_ip": "203.0.113.10", "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0", "comment_content": "Buy cheap pills...", "is_test": false } Response includes: is_spam (boolean) score (0..1) recommendation ( allow , review , discard ) If classification is unavailable, the API returns 503 with error: "detection_unavailable" and no decision. Handle this error explicitly; it does not indicate HAM and does not consume classification usage. Rate Limits ¶ When rate limiting or usage limits apply, the API responds with 429 and a JSON error payload. Next Steps ¶ See the API reference in docs/guides/api-reference.md . Review test mode behavior in docs/guides/test-mode.md .

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ 401 Unauthorized ¶ API key missing or invalid. For dashboard endpoints, ensure the session cookie or Authorization header is present. 429 Too Many Requests ¶ Rate limit exceeded. Monthly usage limit exceeded. 5xx Errors ¶ Retain the request ID from the response when reporting a problem to support. Retry transient failures with a bounded delay and avoid repeated rapid requests. 503 Service Unavailable ¶ HTTP 503 with detection_unavailable means SpamAPI could not complete the spam check. The response contains no spam decision and does not consume classification usage. Keep the submission pending for a later retry or manual review. Do not treat this error as a successful check or as a decision to allow the submission. See the API reference for response and error formats.

docs.text: WordPress Plugin Installation ¶ Requirements ¶ WordPress 6+ PHP 8+ Install ¶ Download the SpamAPI Anti-Spam plugin ZIP . In the WordPress admin, open Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin . Select spamapi-antispam.zip , click Install Now , then Activate Plugin . Open Settings → SpamAPI and paste your dashboard API key. The API URL defaults to https://spamapi.de/api/v1 ; change it only for a self-hosted service. Save the settings, click Test Connection , and enable spam protection. For a manual installation, extract the ZIP and copy its spamapi-antispam folder to wp-content/plugins/ , then activate it from Plugins . The download includes the PHP files, admin assets, and translations needed to run the plugin; no Composer installation is required. Configure ¶ Choose which forms are protected (Comments, CF7, Gravity Forms, WPForms). Enable logging if you need diagnostics.
